salisbury.title: A Simple Method for the Prediction of Therapeutic Proteins (Monoclonal and Polyclonal Antibodies and Non-Antibody Proteins) for First-in-Pediatric Dose Selection: Application of Salisbury Rule
salisbury.text: In order to conduct a pediatric clinical trial, it is crucial to optimize pediatric starting doses as accurately as possible. In this study, a simple weight-based method known as the Salisbury Rule was evaluated to predict pediatric doses for therapeutic proteins and was compared with observed clinical pediatric doses. Prediction accuracy was within 0.5–1.5-fold and 0.7–1.3-fold limits across most sub-populations.
salisbury.citation: Mahmood, I. (2023). Salisbury Rule for Therapeutic Proteins. Antibodies, 12(2), 38.

neonates.title: Prediction of Drug Clearance in Preterm and Term Neonates by Minimal Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Model and Allometry: A Comparison with Whole Body PBPK Model
neonates.text: This investigation compared the predictive performance of a minimal physiologically based pharmacokinetic model (mPBPK) and allometric scaling against a whole-body PBPK model to predict clearance of medications in preterm and term neonates. The minimal PBPK framework demonstrated comparable precision while substantially reducing parameter estimation requirements.
neonates.citation: Mahmood, I. (2023). Drug Clearance in Preterm and Term Neonates. Med Res Arch, 11(8).

adc.title: Allometric Scaling of Clearance for Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs) Across Preclinical Species to Humans
adc.authors: Million Adane Tegenge, Iftekhar Mahmood, Evi Budo Struble, Basil Golding
adc.text: This work evaluated human clearance prediction of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) using 1-, 2-, and 3-species allometric scaling equations. Non-human primate PK data provided the highest fidelity for projecting human clinical ADC clearance.
adc.citation: Tegenge, M. A., Mahmood, I., Struble, E. B., & Golding, B. (2020). Allometric Scaling of ADCs. Antibodies, 9(3), 32.

coagulation.title: Allometric Scaling and Prediction of Concentration-Time Profiles of Coagulation Factors in Humans from Animals
coagulation.text: Allometric scaling was used to project full concentration-time profiles of 5 coagulation factors from preclinical animal models to humans. Predictions closely matched observed patient data, demonstrating utility in hemophilia therapeutic development.
coagulation.citation: Mahmood, I. (2013). Allometric scaling of coagulation factors. Xenobiotica, 43(7), 614-624.
